newsitem.title: DENMARK: Bolstered by dollar, Danish shares hit new record.
newsitem.headline: Bolstered by dollar, Danish shares hit new record.

text.p: The Danish top-20 KFX share index closed at a new record high on Monday, bolstered by the strong dollar, with dealers optimistic about further gains, dependent on the movement of the U.S. currency.
"The dollar broke through an important technical barrier against the mark and depending on the dollar's performance tomorrow we could see more gains," one dealer said.

Earlier in Basle Bundesbank president Hans Tietmeyer said Group of 10 (G10) central bank governors saw no reason to be concerned about currency exchange rates within Europe or between Europe and the U.S. dollar, causing the currency to soar.
The KFX top-20 index finished 2.75 point higher at a new all-time record closing high of 142.44 having earlier in the day hit 142.87 at one point.
Overall bourse turnover was 1.655 billion crowns. The KFX March future rose 1.40 point to 141.00 with 30 contracts each worth 100,000 crowns traded.
Some dealers warned though of possible imminent profit-taking if shares continued their upward surge on Tuesday's U.S. inflation data.
